question: When you sit on a chair, the chair exerts an upward force on you. The reaction force in this case is:
option_1: Your weight acting downward on the chair
option_2: Force of air on the chair
option_3: Friction between your clothes and the chair
solution_text:
The correct answer is Your weight acting downward on the chair.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's third law of motion, every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The chair pushes you upward with a normal reaction force, and in return you push the chair downward with an equal force — this downward push is the reaction force referred to in the question. (न्यूटन का तीसरा नियम — क्रिया-प्रतिक्रिया)

 

• Since you are in equilibrium (not accelerating), this downward force you exert on the chair is equal in magnitude to your weight (mg), which is why it is described as your weight acting downward on the chair.

 

• Action and reaction forces always act on two different bodies (here, the chair and you) and never cancel each other, even though they are equal and opposite.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's first law: a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force (law of inertia).

 

• Newton's second law: F = ma, the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force.

 

• The normal force is a contact force that acts perpendicular to the surface of contact.

 

NOTE

 

• Force of air on the chair (Option B): Irrelevant here; air resistance is negligible in this static situation.

 

• Friction between your clothes and the chair (Option C): Friction acts parallel to the surface, not as the reaction to the normal (upward) force.

 

• Gravitational pull of the Earth (Option D): This is the force causing your weight, but it is not the Newton's-third-law reaction to the chair's push.

question:
Which of the following is true for suspension?

a. Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.

b. The particles of a suspension scatter a beam of light passing through it.

c. The particles of a suspension can be seen by the naked eye.
solution_text:
The correct answer is a, b and c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture in which solute-like particles do not dissolve but remain suspended throughout the medium. (निलंबन — विषमांगी मिश्रण)

 

• The particles of a suspension are large enough to scatter a beam of light passing through them — this is why a suspension appears cloudy/turbid; it also shows the Tyndall effect.

 

• The particles of a suspension are large (more than 1000 nm) and can be seen with the naked eye, unlike a true solution.

 

• All three statements (a, b, c) describing a suspension are correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Suspension particles settle down on standing and can be separated by filtration, unlike true solutions or colloids.

 

• A colloid is intermediate between a solution and a suspension — its particles (1-1000 nm) are too small to be seen by the naked eye but large enough to scatter light (Tyndall effect), and they do not settle on standing.

 

• A true solution (e.g. salt in water) is homogeneous, its particles are less than 1 nm, and it does not scatter light or show the Tyndall effect.

 

NOTE

 

• Options B, C and D are incorrect because they each exclude at least one correct statement — all three given statements about suspensions are factually true.

question: Washing soda is added to water during washing clothes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To make hard water soft.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Washing soda (sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) is added to water while washing clothes because it softens hard water by precipitating out the calcium and magnesium ions responsible for hardness. (धोवन सोडा — जल को मृदु बनाना)

 

• Hard water reacts with soap to form an insoluble scum, which wastes soap and leaves clothes dull; washing soda removes Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions as insoluble carbonates, allowing soap to lather properly.

 

• Washing soda is manufactured by the Solvay process and is also used in the glass, paper and textile industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Baking soda (NaHCO₃, sodium bicarbonate) is a mild antacid and is used in baking and fire extinguishers.

 

• Bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂) is used for bleaching cotton and linen, and for disinfecting drinking water.

 

• Hard water contains dissolved bicarbonates, chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium; it can be temporary (removed by boiling) or permanent (removed only by chemical treatment such as washing soda).

 

NOTE

 

• To add fragrance (Option A): Fragrance in detergents comes from added perfumes, not washing soda.

 

• To prevent wrinkles (Option B): Wrinkle-prevention is unrelated to washing soda's chemical role.

 

• To bleach clothes (Option D): Bleaching is done using bleaching powder or oxidising bleaches, not washing soda.

question: Which of the following methods of asexual reproduction allows a new organism to develop from a cut or broken body part?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fragmentation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fragmentation is a method of asexual reproduction in which the body of a simple multicellular organism breaks into two or more pieces (fragments), and each fragment grows into a new, complete organism. (खंडन — टूटे हुए भाग से नया जीव)

 

• It is seen in simple organisms with a relatively undifferentiated body plan, such as Spirogyra (an aquatic alga) and Planaria (a flatworm), which regenerate lost parts.

 

• This is different from natural growth from a specific bud; here any accidentally cut or broken piece can regenerate an entire new individual.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Spore formation: Reproduction through microscopic reproductive units called spores, seen in Rhizopus (bread mould) and ferns.

 

• Binary fission: A single cell divides into two equal daughter cells, seen in bacteria and Amoeba.

 

• Budding: A new organism develops from a small outgrowth (bud) on the parent's body, seen in yeast and Hydra.

 

• Vegetative propagation is the asexual reproduction of plants from vegetative parts such as roots, stems or leaves (e.g. potato, Bryophyllum).

 

NOTE

 

• Spore formation (Option A): Involves specialised reproductive spores, not a broken body part.

 

• Binary fission (Option B): Involves division of a single cell into two, not fragmentation of a multicellular body.

 

• Budding (Option D): A new individual grows from a specific outgrowth (bud), not from any random cut piece of the body.

question: Which of the following bond is made up of a large number of organic compounds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Covalent bond.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A covalent bond is formed by the mutual sharing of electrons between two atoms, most commonly between carbon atoms and between carbon and other non-metals like hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. (सहसंयोजक बंधन — इलेक्ट्रॉनों का साझा होना)

 

• Because carbon has four valence electrons and can form strong covalent bonds with itself and other elements, the vast majority of organic compounds (compounds of carbon) are held together by covalent bonds.

 

• Covalently bonded organic compounds are generally characterised by low melting and boiling points, poor electrical conductivity, and often exist as gases, liquids or soft solids.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal, forming oppositely charged ions (e.g. NaCl); ionic compounds are typically inorganic, hard, and have high melting points.

 

• Metallic bond is the force of attraction between metal cations and the surrounding 'sea' of delocalised electrons, giving metals their conductivity and malleability.

 

• Carbon's property of forming long chains of covalently bonded atoms with itself is called catenation, which explains the huge diversity of organic compounds.

 

NOTE

 

• Ionic bond (Option A): Typical of inorganic salts, not organic compounds.

 

• Dipolar bond (Option C): Refers to a type of coordinate/polar covalent interaction, not the general bond type of most organic compounds.

 

• Metallic bond (Option D): Found in metals and alloys, not in carbon-based organic molecules.

question: The direction of the magnetic field at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop can be determined by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right-hand rule (curling fingers along current).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The direction of the magnetic field at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop is found using the right-hand rule (also called the right-hand thumb rule): if the fingers of the right hand are curled in the direction of current flow around the loop, the extended thumb points in the direction of the magnetic field at the centre. (दायें हाथ का नियम — धारा की दिशा में उंगलियां मोड़ना)

 

• This rule is a direct consequence of the Biot-Savart law and is used to find the field direction for straight wires, loops and solenoids alike.

 

• For a straight current-carrying conductor, the same right-hand rule (thumb along current, curled fingers show field direction around the wire) applies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fleming's left-hand rule is used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field (motor effect) — thumb=force, first finger=field, second finger=current.

 

• Fleming's right-hand rule is used to find the direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field (generator effect).

 

• The strength of the magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop is directly proportional to the current and the number of turns, and inversely proportional to the radius.

 

NOTE

 

• Right-hand palm rule (Option A): Not the standard named rule for this situation; often confused terminology.

 

• Left-hand thumb rule (Option B): Not applicable here — the left-hand rule (Fleming's) is used for force, not field direction from current.

 

• Fleming's left-hand rule (Option C): Used for finding force on a conductor in a field, not the field due to current itself.

question: Which of the following is NOT necessary for work to be done on a body?
option_2: A force must be applied on the body.
option_3: The body must move at a constant speed.
option_4: The force must have a component along the direction of displacement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The body must move at a constant speed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In physics, work done (W) = F × d × cosθ, where F is the applied force, d is the displacement, and θ is the angle between force and displacement. (कार्य = बल × विस्थापन × cosθ)

 

• For work to be done, three conditions are essential: a force must act on the body, the body must undergo a displacement, and the force must have a component along the displacement (θ ≠ 90°).

 

• The speed at which the body moves — whether constant, increasing or decreasing — has no bearing on whether work is being done; only force and displacement (and the angle between them) matter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• If the force is perpendicular to displacement (θ = 90°), work done is zero — e.g. a person carrying a load horizontally does no work against gravity.

 

• The SI unit of work is the joule (J), equal to 1 newton-metre.

 

• Work done by friction on a moving body is negative because the frictional force acts opposite to the direction of displacement.

 

NOTE

 

• The body must get displaced (Option A): This is genuinely necessary — without displacement, no work is done even if a force acts.

 

• A force must be applied (Option B): Necessary — work cannot be done without an applied force.

 

• The force must have a component along displacement (Option D): Necessary — a force entirely perpendicular to displacement does zero work.

question:
Read the given statements as select the most appropriate option.

Statements:

A: Small bulb like projection from yeast cell is bud.

B: Chain of bud formation is found in the budding process of yeast.
option_1: Both Statement A and Statement B are correct
option_2: Both Statement A and Statement B are incorrect
option_3: Statement A is correct and Statement B is incorrect
option_4: Statement B is correct and Statement A is incorrect
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both Statement A and Statement B are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement A is correct: In yeast, a small bulb-like outgrowth (projection) develops on the parent cell, which is called a bud; this is the structure from which budding occurs. (नवोदित होना — मुकुल)

 

• Statement B is correct: As new buds keep forming on the parent cell (and sometimes on the daughter buds themselves before they detach), they can remain attached and form a chain-like or branched structure, a phenomenon commonly seen during rapid budding in yeast.

 

• Both statements accurately describe the process of budding, a form of asexual reproduction seen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) and Hydra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• In Hydra, budding produces a single bud that grows tentacles and detaches as an independent organism, unlike the chain formation sometimes seen in yeast.

 

• Binary fission in yeast can also occur under some conditions, but budding is its characteristic mode of asexual reproduction.

 

• Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring (clones) since only one parent is involved, and no gametes fuse.

 

NOTE

 

• Options B, C and D are incorrect because both given statements about budding in yeast are factually accurate.

question: When a gun is fired, why does the gun experience a recoil even though the bullet moves forward?
option_1: Because the gun pushes the bullet forward with less force
option_2: Because the gun's mass is smaller than the bullet's
option_3: Because the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun
option_4: Because the bullet's acceleration is less than the gun's
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The recoil of a gun is a direct application of Newton's third law of motion: when the gun exerts a forward force on the bullet, the bullet simultaneously exerts an equal and opposite (backward) force on the gun. (बंदूक का प्रतिक्षेप — न्यूटन का तीसरा नियम)

 

• This phenomenon is also explained by the law of conservation of momentum: before firing, the total momentum of the gun-bullet system is zero; after firing, the forward momentum gained by the bullet is exactly balanced by the backward momentum gained by the gun.

 

• Since the gun's mass is much larger than the bullet's, for the same magnitude of momentum, the gun's recoil velocity is much smaller than the bullet's forward velocity (v = p/m).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Momentum conservation: m₁v₁ = m₂v₂ (momentum of bullet forward = momentum of gun backward, in magnitude), which is why heavier guns produce less noticeable recoil.

 

• Momentum (p = mv) is a vector quantity, with SI unit kg m/s.

 

• The recoil principle is also used in rocket propulsion, where hot gases are expelled backward, propelling the rocket forward.

 

NOTE

 

• Gun pushes bullet with less force (Option A): Incorrect — by Newton's third law, the forces on the gun and bullet are always exactly equal in magnitude.

 

• Gun's mass is smaller than bullet's (Option B): Factually wrong — the gun's mass is far greater than the bullet's.

 

• Bullet's acceleration is less than gun's (Option D): Incorrect — since the bullet has much smaller mass, for the same force it experiences much greater acceleration than the gun.

question: Which of the following types of animal husbandry helps us in honey production?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bee-keeping.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bee-keeping, also called apiculture, is the branch of animal husbandry concerned with rearing honeybees in hives for the commercial production of honey and beeswax. (मधुमक्खी पालन — मधु उत्पादन)

 

• Honeybees also play a vital ecological role as pollinators, increasing crop yield in many flowering plants, making apiculture doubly beneficial for farmers.

 

• Common honeybee species reared in India include Apis cerana indica, Apis mellifera and Apis dorsata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Animal husbandry is the branch of agricultural science dealing with the scientific management and breeding of livestock, including cattle, poultry, fisheries and bees.

 

• Pisciculture (fish farming) deals with the commercial rearing of fish; culture fishery refers to fish farming in controlled water bodies.

 

• Poultry farming deals with rearing birds like chickens, ducks and turkeys for eggs and meat.

 

NOTE

 

• Cattle farming (Option A): Concerned with rearing cows and buffaloes, mainly for milk, meat and draught power.

 

• Culture fishery (Option B): Concerned with rearing fish in ponds/tanks for food production, not honey.

 

• Poultry (Option D): Concerned with rearing birds for eggs and meat, not honey.

question: What is the network of tiny tubular structures found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Endoplasmic reticulum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a large network of membrane-bound tubules and flattened sacs (cisternae) that extends throughout the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell, connecting the nuclear membrane to the cell membrane. (अंतर्द्रव्यी जालिका — नलिकाओं का जाल)

 

• There are two types: Rough ER (RER), studded with ribosomes and involved in protein synthesis, and Smooth ER (SER), which helps in lipid/steroid synthesis and detoxification.

 

• The ER also acts as a channel for the intracellular transport of materials and provides structural support (cytoskeletal framework) to the cytoplasm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mitochondria are double-membraned, rod-shaped organelles known as the 'powerhouse of the cell', producing ATP through cellular respiration.

 

• Golgi apparatus consists of stacks of flattened sacs and is responsible for packaging, modifying and dispatching materials (like a cell's 'post office').

 

• Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicles containing digestive enzymes and are known as the 'suicide bags' of the cell.

 

NOTE

 

• Mitochondria (Option A): The energy-producing organelle, not a tubular network for transport.

 

• Lysosome (Option B): A digestive/waste-disposal vesicle, not a tubular network.

 

• Golgi apparatus (Option C): A stack of sac-like structures for packaging, distinct in shape from the ER's tubular network.

question: The smell of hot food reaches a distance because:
option_4: sound waves carry the food smell
solution_text:
The correct answer is particles are continuously moving.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the kinetic theory of matter, all particles of matter are constantly and randomly in motion; this motion is what causes the aroma (odorous gas particles) of hot food to spread through the air and reach us — a process called diffusion. (कण गति — विसरण)

 

• Diffusion is faster in gases than in liquids or solids because gas particles have more space between them and move much faster.

 

• Since hot food has particles with higher kinetic energy, its smell spreads (diffuses) faster and farther than that of cold food.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three states of matter — solid, liquid and gas — differ in the arrangement and motion of their particles: gas particles are farthest apart and move fastest, while solid particles are closely packed and vibrate about fixed positions.

 

• Diffusion in gases explains many everyday phenomena, such as the smell of perfume spreading in a room or the mixing of gases without stirring.

 

• Increasing temperature increases the average kinetic energy of particles, speeding up diffusion.

 

NOTE

 

• Temperature increases food weight (Option A): Physically incorrect; temperature does not add mass to food.

 

• Light energy spreads aroma particles (Option B): Light has no role in the diffusion of smell particles.

 

• Sound waves carry the food smell (Option D): Sound is a mechanical wave and does not transport chemical (odour) particles.

question: A sound wave has a frequency of 250 Hz. The time taken for one complete vibration is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.004 s (printed in the source as Option C, "C).004 s").

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The time period (T) of a wave is the time taken for one complete vibration/oscillation, and it is the reciprocal of frequency: T = 1/f. (आवर्तकाल = 1/आवृत्ति)

 

• Here, frequency f = 250 Hz, so T = 1/250 = 0.004 seconds.

 

• Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), defined as one vibration/cycle per second, named after Heinrich Hertz.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wave equation: Speed of sound (v) = frequency (f) × wavelength (λ).

 

• The audible range for humans is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; sounds below this are infrasonic and above it are ultrasonic.

 

• Speed of sound in air at room temperature is about 344 m/s; it travels faster in solids and liquids than in gases.

 

NOTE

 

• Option A (0.40 s) and Option D (0.25 s) would correspond to much lower frequencies (2.5 Hz and 4 Hz respectively), not 250 Hz.

 

• Option B (0.0 s) is not a physically meaningful time period for a wave of finite frequency.

question: What happens to a light ray when it passes through the optical centre of a lens?
option_1: It will emerge parallel to the principal axis
option_2: It passes through the principal focus on the other side of the lens
option_3: It will emerge without any deviation
option_4: It bends toward the principal axis
solution_text:
The correct answer is It will emerge without any deviation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The optical centre of a lens is the central point through which a ray of light passes without any deviation (undeviated), continuing in the same straight-line direction. (प्रकाशिक केंद्र — बिना विचलन के गमन)

 

• This is one of the three standard rules used to trace ray diagrams for lenses, and it holds true for both convex and concave lenses.

 

• This rule is used along with two others to locate the position and nature of images formed by lenses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rule 2: A ray parallel to the principal axis, after refraction, passes through the principal focus (for a convex lens) or appears to diverge from it (for a concave lens).

 

• Rule 3: A ray passing through the principal focus, after refraction, emerges parallel to the principal axis.

 

• The power of a lens (P = 1/f) is measured in dioptre (D); convex lenses have positive power and concave lenses have negative power.

 

NOTE

 

• Emerge parallel to principal axis (Option A): This describes a ray originally passing through the focus, not through the optical centre.

 

• Passes through principal focus (Option B): This describes a ray originally parallel to the principal axis, not one through the optical centre.

 

• Bends toward the principal axis (Option D): Incorrect — a ray through the optical centre does not bend at all.

question: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaSO₄·½H₂O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plaster of Paris (POP) has the chemical formula CaSO₄·½H₂O (calcium sulphate hemihydrate). (प्लास्टर ऑफ पेरिस — CaSO₄·½H₂O)

 

• It is prepared by heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) to about 373 K (100°C), which drives off three-quarters of its water of crystallisation.

 

• When mixed with water, Plaster of Paris sets into a hard mass by re-absorbing water and reverting back to gypsum; this property makes it useful for making moulds, casts for setting fractured bones, and toys.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plaster of Paris must be stored in moisture-proof containers, as exposure to atmospheric moisture would cause it to set even before use.

 

• The reaction of setting: CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O (gypsum, hard solid mass).

 

• Gypsum is also used to make cement and as a fertiliser (soil conditioner) to correct alkaline soils.

 

NOTE

 

• CaCO₃ (Option A): This is calcium carbonate — found in limestone, chalk and marble; not the formula of Plaster of Paris.

 

• CaSO₄ (Option C): This is anhydrous calcium sulphate (formed if gypsum is overheated), not Plaster of Paris itself.

 

• CaSO₄·2H₂O (Option D): This is gypsum, the raw material from which Plaster of Paris is made, not POP itself.

question: A concave mirror can form a real and inverted image when the object is placed:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beyond the centre of curvature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A concave mirror forms a real and inverted image for any object placed beyond the focus (F) — this includes when the object is beyond the centre of curvature (C), in which case the image forms between F and C, is real, inverted and diminished. (अवतल दर्पण — वास्तविक व उल्टा प्रतिबिंब)

 

• When the object is placed exactly at C, the image also forms at C, real, inverted and of the same size.

 

• When the object is placed between F and C, the image forms beyond C, real, inverted and magnified.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• If the object is placed at the focus (F), the reflected rays become parallel and the image forms at infinity.

 

• If the object is placed between the pole and focus, the image formed is virtual, erect and magnified — this is why concave mirrors are used as shaving/makeup mirrors.

 

• Concave (converging) mirrors are also used in torches, headlights, and solar cookers to concentrate light.

 

NOTE

 

• At the focus (Option A): Produces an image at infinity, not a well-defined real inverted image at a finite distance.

 

• Between focus and pole (Option C): Produces a virtual, erect, magnified image, not a real inverted one.

 

• Very close to the mirror (Option D): Also falls within the focus-to-pole range, giving a virtual, erect image.

question: A school organises a 'Zero Waste' day. Which of the following practices will best support this initiative?
option_3: Disposing food waste in regular trash bins
option_4: Serving food in banana leaves or reusable plates
solution_text:
The correct answer is Serving food in banana leaves or reusable plates.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A 'Zero Waste' initiative aims to minimise the amount of waste (especially non-biodegradable waste) sent to landfills by promoting reuse, recycling and biodegradable alternatives. (शून्य अपशिष्ट — पुन:प्रयोज्य विकल्प)

 

• Banana leaves are fully biodegradable and reusable plates eliminate single-use waste altogether, making this the practice most aligned with a zero-waste goal.

 

• The other three options all involve single-use plastics or unsegregated disposal, which directly work against a zero-waste philosophy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The '3 Rs' of waste management are Reduce, Reuse, Recycle; some frameworks add a fourth R — Refuse (avoiding unnecessary waste-generating products).

 

• Biodegradable waste (like food scraps, leaves) decomposes naturally through microbial action, while non-biodegradable waste (like most plastics) persists in the environment for decades.

 

• India's Single-Use Plastics ban (effective 2022) prohibits several categories of disposable plastic items, including plastic cutlery and thin plastic bags.

 

NOTE

 

• Wrapping snacks in plastic foil (Option A): Generates non-biodegradable plastic waste.

 

• Using single-use plastic cutlery (Option B): Directly contradicts a zero-waste, single-use-plastic-free approach.

 

• Disposing food waste in regular trash bins (Option C): Fails to segregate biodegradable waste for composting, a key part of waste minimisation.

question: Which of the following characteristics of connective tissue is INCORRECT?
option_1: Cells are embedded in an intercellular matrix.
option_2: Blood is a type of connective tissue.
option_3: Matrix may be jelly-like, fluid, dense or rigid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cells are tightly arranged.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Connective tissue is characterised by having relatively few, loosely (sparsely) arranged cells embedded within a large amount of intercellular matrix, which is exactly the opposite of the statement 'cells are tightly arranged'. (संयोजी ऊतक — कोशिकाएं शिथिल रूप से व्यवस्थित)

 

• The matrix may vary in consistency — it can be jelly-like (areolar tissue), fluid (blood plasma), dense (tendons, ligaments) or rigid/mineralised (bone) — depending on the type of connective tissue.

 

• Blood is indeed classified as a specialised fluid connective tissue, as its cells (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) are suspended in a fluid matrix called plasma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major types of connective tissue: areolar tissue (packing between organs), adipose tissue (fat storage), bone, cartilage, tendons (muscle to bone), ligaments (bone to bone) and blood.

 

• Cartilage has a solid but flexible matrix and lacks blood vessels; it cushions joints and forms parts of the nose, ear and trachea.

 

• Connective tissue functions include binding, support, protection and transport (in the case of blood).

 

NOTE

 

• Cells embedded in an intercellular matrix (Option A): A correct, defining feature of connective tissue.

 

• Blood is a type of connective tissue (Option B): Correct — blood is classified as fluid connective tissue.

 

• Matrix may be jelly-like, fluid, dense or rigid (Option C): Correct — matrix consistency varies widely across connective tissue types.

question: Which of the following elements shows +2 valency?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beryllium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Beryllium (Be), atomic number 4, belongs to Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) of the periodic table and has 2 electrons in its outermost shell; it loses both to attain a stable configuration, showing a valency of +2. (बेरिलियम — संयोजकता +2)

 

• Elements of Group 2 (Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba) characteristically show a +2 valency by losing their two valence electrons.

 

• Beryllium's electronic configuration is 2, 2, so it readily loses its 2 outer electrons to form the Be²⁺ ion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hydrogen shows a valency of +1 (or -1 in metal hydrides), as it has only 1 electron.

 

• Lithium (Group 1, alkali metal) shows a valency of +1, losing its single valence electron.

 

• Helium is a noble gas with a completely filled outer shell (2 electrons), so it is chemically inert and shows a valency of 0.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogen (Option A): Shows +1 valency, not +2.

 

• Lithium (Option B): An alkali metal showing +1 valency.

 

• Helium (Option D): A noble gas with zero valency due to its stable, filled electron shell.

question: Which of the following explains a precipitation reaction?
option_1: A reaction where heat is released
option_2: A reaction involving a color change only
option_3: A reaction in which a gas is formed
option_4: A reaction where an insoluble solid is formed
solution_text:
The correct answer is A reaction where an insoluble solid is formed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A precipitation reaction is a type of chemical reaction, usually a double displacement reaction, in which two soluble salts react in an aqueous solution to form an insoluble solid (precipitate) that settles out. (अवक्षेपण अभिक्रिया — अघुलनशील ठोस बनना)

 

• A classic example is: Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s)↓ + 2NaCl(aq), where the white insoluble barium sulphate precipitates out.

 

• The defining feature of a precipitation reaction is specifically the formation of this insoluble solid, not simply a colour change or heat release, though these may sometimes accompany it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Exothermic reactions release heat (e.g. combustion, respiration); endothermic reactions absorb heat (e.g. photosynthesis).

 

• A reaction producing a gas (like the reaction of a metal with an acid producing hydrogen gas) is a distinct category, not automatically a precipitation reaction.

 

• Double displacement reactions involve the exchange of ions between two reacting compounds; if one product is insoluble, it is termed a precipitation reaction.

 

NOTE

 

• Heat is released (Option A): Describes an exothermic reaction, a different classification from precipitation.

 

• Color change only (Option B): May occur in many reaction types but does not define precipitation.

 

• A gas is formed (Option C): Describes gas-evolving reactions, not precipitation reactions.

question: Which of the following is true about the universal gravitational constant G?
option_1: It is equal to the acceleration due to gravity.
option_2: It depends on the medium between two masses.
option_3: It is a universal constant, same everywhere.
option_4: It varies from place to place on Earth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is a universal constant, same everywhere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The universal gravitational constant (G), introduced in Newton's law of universal gravitation (F = Gm₁m₂/r²), has the same fixed value everywhere in the universe, independent of the masses, the medium, or location. (गुरुत्वाकर्षण स्थिरांक — सार्वत्रिक रूप से स्थिर)

 

• Its value is G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², first experimentally determined by Henry Cavendish in 1798.

 

• G does not depend on the medium between the two masses, unlike some other physical constants that vary with the medium (e.g. permittivity in electrostatics).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• In contrast, acceleration due to gravity (g) is not a universal constant — it varies with location (maximum at poles, minimum at the equator) and depends on the mass and radius of the attracting body (g = GM/R²).

 

• On the Moon, g is about one-sixth of its value on Earth, while G would still be exactly the same.

 

• G is used to calculate the mass of celestial bodies, escape velocity, and orbital motion of planets and satellites.

 

NOTE

 

• Equal to acceleration due to gravity (Option A): Incorrect — G and g are entirely different physical quantities with different units and values.

 

• Depends on the medium (Option B): Incorrect — G is independent of any intervening medium.

 

• Varies from place to place on Earth (Option D): This describes g, not G, which remains constant everywhere.

question: The equivalent resistance in a parallel combination is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is smaller than the smallest resistance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a parallel combination of resistors, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance equals the sum of the reciprocals of individual resistances: 1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + .... (समांतर क्रम — तुल्य प्रतिरोध सबसे छोटे प्रतिरोध से भी कम)

 

• Because of this reciprocal relationship, the equivalent resistance of a parallel combination is always smaller than the smallest individual resistance in the combination.

 

• This happens because adding more parallel paths provides more routes for current to flow, effectively decreasing overall opposition to current flow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a series combination, the equivalent resistance is the sum of all individual resistances: R_eq = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + ..., and it is always greater than the largest individual resistance.

 

• Household electrical circuits are wired in parallel so that each appliance gets the same voltage and can operate independently (one device failing does not affect others).

 

• Ohm's Law: V = IR, relates voltage, current and resistance; resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

 

NOTE

 

• Sum of all resistances (Option A): This describes series combination, not parallel.

 

• Greater than the largest resistance (Option B): This describes the behaviour of series combination.

 

• Equal to the largest resistance (Option C): Incorrect for both series and parallel combinations in general.

question: Which of the following statements about meristematic tissues is INCORRECT?
option_1: Cells are small, thin-walled, and densely cytoplasmic with large nuclei.
option_3: Meristematic tissues consist of actively dividing cells.
option_4: Meristematic cells are dead at maturity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meristematic cells are dead at maturity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meristematic tissue consists of cells that are always living and capable of continuous active division; the statement that they are 'dead at maturity' is factually incorrect. (विभज्योतक ऊतक — सदैव जीवित, विभाजनशील कोशिकाएं)

 

• (Being dead at maturity is instead a feature of certain permanent tissues, such as xylem vessels/tracheids and cork cells, which lose their protoplasm once mature.)

 

• Meristematic cells are typically small, thin-walled, with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, and lack a large central vacuole, allowing rapid division.

 

• Meristematic tissue is responsible for lifelong (perpetual) growth in plants, unlike animals whose growth typically stops after a certain age.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Types of meristem by location: apical meristem (at root and shoot tips, increases length), lateral meristem (e.g. vascular cambium, cork cambium — increases girth) and intercalary meristem (at the base of leaves/internodes, e.g. in grasses).

 

• Cells produced by meristematic tissue differentiate into permanent tissues (simple: parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma; complex: xylem, phloem), which lose the ability to divide.

 

NOTE

 

• Small, thin-walled, densely cytoplasmic with large nuclei (Option A): A correct description of meristematic cells.

 

• Enable lifelong growth in plants (Option B): Correct — this is the defining function of meristematic tissue.

 

• Consist of actively dividing cells (Option C): Correct — continuous cell division is the hallmark of meristematic tissue.

question: Which of the following is a property of suspension?
option_1: Solute particles cannot be separated by the process of filtration
option_3: Particles cannot be seen by naked eyes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture in which relatively large, insoluble particles are dispersed throughout a liquid (or gas) medium but do not dissolve in it. (निलंबन — विषमांगी मिश्रण)

 

• Suspension particles are large enough to be seen by the naked eye, they settle down on standing, and they can be separated by simple filtration — the exact opposite of what the other three options claim.

 

• A common example is muddy water, where the suspended soil particles are visible and gradually settle at the bottom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• True solutions (e.g. sugar or salt dissolved in water) are homogeneous, and their solute particles cannot be separated by filtration and do not settle.

 

• Colloids are intermediate: particles are too small to see individually but large enough to scatter light (Tyndall effect); they do not settle on standing and cannot be separated by ordinary filtration (require centrifugation).

 

• The size of suspension particles is typically greater than 1000 nm (1 micrometre).

 

NOTE

 

• Solute particles cannot be separated by filtration (Option A): This describes true solutions, not suspensions (suspension particles CAN be filtered out).

 

• Particles do not settle (Option B): Incorrect for suspensions — their particles do settle over time.

 

• Particles cannot be seen by naked eyes (Option C): Incorrect — suspension particles are large enough to be visible to the naked eye.

question: Which one of the following is NOT an agent of cross pollination?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Light.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of a flower on a different plant, and it requires an external carrying agent to transport the pollen. (परागण के अभिकर्ता)

 

• Common natural agents of pollination include wind (anemophily), water (hydrophily), and animals such as insects, birds and bats (biotic pollination, e.g. entomophily by insects, ornithophily by birds).

 

• Light has no physical role in carrying pollen from one flower to another and is therefore not a pollinating agent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wind-pollinated flowers (e.g. grasses, maize) typically produce large amounts of light, dry, non-sticky pollen and often lack showy petals or fragrance.

 

• Insect-pollinated flowers are typically brightly coloured, fragrant, and produce nectar to attract pollinators such as bees and butterflies.

 

• Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or between flowers of the same plant, and does not require an external agent.

 

NOTE

 

• Wind (Option A): A well-known abiotic agent of cross-pollination (anemophily).

 

• Water (Option B): An abiotic agent of pollination in aquatic plants (hydrophily), e.g. Vallisneria.

 

• Animals (Option D): The most common biotic agents of cross-pollination, including insects, birds and bats.

question: The ratio of the two sides of a rectangle is 2 : 3. If the area of the rectangle is 2646 cm², then its perimeter is ______ cm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 210.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ratio of sides = 2 : 3; Area = 2646 cm².

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the sides be 2x and 3x. Area = 2x × 3x = 6x² = 2646.

 

• x² = 2646 ÷ 6 = 441 ⇒ x = 21.

 

• Sides = 2(21) = 42 cm and 3(21) = 63 cm.

 

• Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 2(42 + 63) = 2 × 105 = 210 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For ratio a : b and area A, side unit x = √(A/(ab)); here x = √(2646/6) = √441 = 21; perimeter = 2x(a+b) = 2×21×5 = 210.

 

NOTE

 

• Always find the value of the ratio unit (x) first using the area, then compute the actual dimensions before applying the perimeter formula.

question: Two outlet pipes, A and B, can separately empty a full tank in 17 hours and 15 hours, respectively. Both the outlet pipes are opened together for 'x' hours. Had outlet pipe B been opened alone, it would have taken (x + 5) hours to empty the same quantity of water from the tank. What is the value of x?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 5⅔.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pipe A empties the tank in 17 h, pipe B in 15 h. A and B together work for x hours; the same quantity emptied would take B alone (x + 5) hours.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Combined rate of A and B = 1/17 + 1/15 = (15 + 17)/255 = 32/255 (of tank per hour).

 

• Quantity emptied by A and B together in x hours = (32/255)x.

 

• This equals the quantity B alone empties in (x+5) hours = (1/15)(x+5).

 

• So (32/255)x = (x+5)/15. Multiplying both sides by 255: 32x = 17(x+5) [since 255/15 = 17].

 

• 32x = 17x + 85 ⇒ 15x = 85 ⇒ x = 85/15 = 17/3 = 5⅔ hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up 'work by A+B in x hours' = 'work by B alone in (x+5) hours' directly as an equation in rates; cross-multiply by the LCM of the times to avoid fractions.

 

NOTE

 

• Always express 'quantity of work done' as rate × time, and equate the two expressions for the *same* quantity of water emptied.

question: From the top of a tower of height 10 m, a boy observes a car on the ground moving away from the base of the tower. If the angle of depression of the car changes from 60° to 30°, how far has the car moved during this time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. (10√3 − 10/√3) m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Height of tower = 10 m; angle of depression changes from 60° to 30° as the car moves away.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the two positions of the car be at distances x₁ (at 60°) and x₂ (at 30°) from the base of the tower.

 

• At 60°: tan60° = height/x₁ ⇒ √3 = 10/x₁ ⇒ x₁ = 10/√3.

 

• At 30°: tan30° = height/x₂ ⇒ 1/√3 = 10/x₂ ⇒ x₂ = 10√3.

 

• Distance moved = x₂ − x₁ = 10√3 − 10/√3 = (10√3 − 10/√3) m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Distance moved = h(cot(smaller angle) − cot(larger angle)) = 10(cot30° − cot60°) = 10(√3 − 1/√3).

 

NOTE

 

• As the angle of depression decreases, the object is moving farther away; always take (distance at smaller angle) − (distance at larger angle).

question:
Walking at ⅔rd of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 18 minutes late in reaching his office.

The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 36 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• New speed = ⅔ of normal speed; this makes Abhijeet 18 minutes late.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since speed and time are inversely proportional, if speed becomes ⅔, time becomes 3/2 (i.e., 1½ times) of the usual time.

 

• Extra time taken = (3/2 − 1) × usual time = (1/2) × usual time = 18 minutes.

 

• Usual time = 18 × 2 = 36 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If speed becomes a/b of the usual, extra time = (b/a − 1) × usual time = (b−a)/a × usual time. Here (3−2)/2 × T = 18 ⇒ T = 36.

 

NOTE

 

• Speed and time are inversely proportional for a fixed distance — never add/subtract speeds and times directly.

question: The income of Raman is ₹49,000. He saves 27.5% of his income. If his income increases by 34% and expenditure increases by 20%, then his savings will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. increase by ₹9,555.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income = ₹49,000; savings = 27.5% of income; new income is 34% more, new expenditure is 20% more than old expenditure.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Old savings = 27.5% of 49,000 = 0.275 × 49,000 = ₹13,475.

 

• Old expenditure = 49,000 − 13,475 = ₹35,525.

 

• New income = 49,000 × 1.34 = ₹65,660.

 

• New expenditure = 35,525 × 1.20 = ₹42,630.

 

• New savings = 65,660 − 42,630 = ₹23,030.

 

• Change in savings = 23,030 − 13,475 = increase of ₹9,555.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• New savings = New income − New expenditure; always compute new income and new expenditure separately rather than trying to scale the savings percentage directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Income, expenditure and savings percentages don't scale the same way — income and expenditure changes must each be applied to their own base value.

question: A class of 78 students took a Physics test. 17 students had an average score of 70. The remaining students had an average score of 90. What is the average score (rounded off to one decimal place) of the whole class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 85.6 (printed in the source as "C).6").

 

GIVEN

 

• Total students = 78; 17 students average = 70; remaining (78 − 17 = 61) students average = 90.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total score of 17 students = 17 × 70 = 1,190.

 

• Total score of remaining 61 students = 61 × 90 = 5,490.

 

• Total score of whole class = 1,190 + 5,490 = 6,680.

 

• Average of whole class = 6,680 ÷ 78 = 85.641... ≈ 85.6 (rounded to one decimal place).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Weighted average = (Σ(count × average of each group)) ÷ total count; always weight each group's average by its own count, not by a simple average of the two averages.

 

NOTE

 

• The printed options here carry an OCR-style artefact (e.g. "C).6"), representing the decimal-place digit of the computed average 85.6 — the full computed value 85.6 is what determines the correct option.

question:
If 9 is subtracted from the numerator of a fraction, it becomes 2/9, and if 12 is added to the denominator of the fraction, it becomes 1/3.

What is the sum of the numerator and the denominator of the original fraction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 64.

 

GIVEN

 

• Let the fraction be n/d. (n − 9)/d = 2/9, and n/(d + 12) = 1/3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• From (n − 9)/d = 2/9: 9(n − 9) = 2d ⇒ 9n − 81 = 2d ... (i)

 

• From n/(d + 12) = 1/3: 3n = d + 12 ⇒ d = 3n − 12 ... (ii)

 

• Substituting (ii) into (i): 9n − 81 = 2(3n − 12) = 6n − 24 ⇒ 9n − 6n = 81 − 24 ⇒ 3n = 57 ⇒ n = 19.

 

• d = 3(19) − 12 = 57 − 12 = 45.

 

• Sum = n + d = 19 + 45 = 64.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert both conditions into linear equations in n and d, then solve simultaneously by substitution — always verify by plugging n, d back into both original conditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Check: (19−9)/45 = 10/45 = 2/9 ✓; 19/(45+12) = 19/57 = 1/3 ✓.

question: The average age of 38 students of a class is 21 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 22 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 60.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 38 students = 21 years; average age of 39 people (including teacher) = 22 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total age of 38 students = 38 × 21 = 798 years.

 

• Total age of 39 people (students + teacher) = 39 × 22 = 858 years.

 

• Teacher's age = 858 − 798 = 60 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = new average + (number of students × increase in average) = 22 + (38 × 1) = 22 + 38 = 60.

 

NOTE

 

• When one new member changes the average of a group, the new member's value = new average + (old count × increase in average).

question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at X% above the cost price and sells them at a discount of 48%. If he makes a profit of 82%, find the value of X.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 250.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price = CP × (1 + X/100); discount = 48%; profit = 82%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Selling Price (from profit) = CP × (1 + 82/100) = 1.82 × CP.

 

• Selling Price (from marked price and discount) = MP × (1 − 48/100) = (1 + X/100) × CP × 0.52.

 

• Equating: (1 + X/100) × 0.52 = 1.82 ⇒ 1 + X/100 = 1.82/0.52 = 3.5.

 

• X/100 = 3.5 − 1 = 2.5 ⇒ X = 250.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• (1 + Markup%) × (1 − Discount%) = (1 + Profit%); plug in known values and solve for the unknown percentage directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always express markup, discount and profit as multiplying factors on the cost price — this avoids sign errors when combining them.

question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7.5% per annum, respectively. Manjit borrowed an amount of ₹2,20,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Manjit after 2 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 17,600.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal = ₹2,20,000 (each bank); Rate A = 3.5% p.a.; Rate B = 7.5% p.a.; Time = 2 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• SI = (P × R × T)/100.

 

• SI to Bank A = (2,20,000 × 3.5 × 2)/100 = ₹15,400.

 

• SI to Bank B = (2,20,000 × 7.5 × 2)/100 = ₹33,000.

 

• Difference = 33,000 − 15,400 = ₹17,600.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since principal and time are the same for both, difference in SI = P × T × (difference in rates)/100 = 2,20,000 × 2 × 4/100 = ₹17,600.

 

NOTE

 

• When principal and time are common to both loans, work directly with the difference of rates instead of calculating each SI separately.

question: The HCF of ½, ¾, 27/16 and 81/64 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1/64.

 

GIVEN

 

• Fractions: 1/2, 3/4, 27/16, 81/64.

 

SOLUTION

 

• HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators.

 

• Numerators: 1, 3, 27, 81 → HCF(1, 3, 27, 81) = 1.

 

• Denominators: 2, 4, 16, 64 → LCM(2, 4, 16, 64) = 64.

 

• HCF of the fractions = 1/64.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For fractions, HCF = HCF(numerators)/LCM(denominators), and LCM = LCM(numerators)/HCF(denominators) — memorise both formulas as they are frequently swapped in wrong options.

 

NOTE

 

• Since the numerators here (1, 3, 27, 81) share no common factor greater than 1, their HCF is simply 1, making the fractions' HCF the smallest possible value, 1/64.

question: During a New-Year sale, a company gives a 'Buy 9 Sweaters and Get 1 Free' offer to customers. The percentage discount involved in this deal is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 10%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Offer: Buy 9 sweaters, get 1 free (i.e., pay for 9, receive 10).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Customer pays the price of 9 sweaters but receives 10 sweaters (equivalent to a free sweater's worth of discount on 10 sweaters).

 

• Discount % = (Number of free items ÷ Total items received) × 100 = (1/10) × 100 = 10%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 'Buy n, Get 1 Free' offers, discount % = [1/(n+1)] × 100. Here n = 9, so discount = 1/10 × 100 = 10%.

 

NOTE

 

• Always divide the free quantity by the *total* items received (paid + free), not by the number of items paid for.

question: The radii of two cylinders is in the ratio 3 : 4 and their heights is in the ratio 5 : 2. The ratio of their volumes will be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 45 : 32.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ratio of radii r₁ : r₂ = 3 : 4; ratio of heights h₁ : h₂ = 5 : 2.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of a cylinder = πr²h, so ratio of volumes = (r₁²h₁) : (r₂²h₂).

 

• = (3² × 5) : (4² × 2) = (9 × 5) : (16 × 2) = 45 : 32.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Volume ratio for cylinders = (ratio of radii)² × (ratio of heights); apply the square only to the radius ratio, not the height ratio.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is squaring both the radius and height ratios — remember only radius is squared in the volume formula πr²h.

question: If p : q : r = 8 : 5 : 12 and r : s = 36 : 18, then what is the value of p : q : r : s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 24:15:36:18.

 

GIVEN

 

• p : q : r = 8 : 5 : 12; r : s = 36 : 18.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Simplify r : s = 36 : 18 = 2 : 1.

 

• To combine, make the value of r equal in both ratios. In p:q:r, r = 12; multiply this entire ratio by 3 to get r = 36: p:q:r = 24:15:36.

 

• Now r:s = 36:18 already has r = 36, matching directly.

 

• Combined ratio: p : q : r : s = 24 : 15 : 36 : 18.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To combine two ratios sharing a common term, scale each ratio (using LCM of the common term's two values) until the common term matches exactly, then merge.

 

NOTE

 

• Here LCM(12, 36) = 36, so the first ratio was multiplied by 3 (36÷12) and the second needed no change (36 was already the r-value).

question: An article is sold at a gain of 30%. Had it been sold for ₹48 more, the profit would have been 35%. The cost price of the article is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹960.

 

GIVEN

 

• Selling at 30% profit vs. selling at 35% profit differ by ₹48 in selling price.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Difference in profit percentage = 35% − 30% = 5% of CP.

 

• 5% of CP = ₹48.

 

• CP = 48 × (100/5) = 48 × 20 = ₹960.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a fixed rupee difference in SP corresponds to a difference in profit %, that rupee amount equals (difference in %) of the CP — divide directly to get CP.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse this with a percentage of SP; the extra ₹48 corresponds to extra % profit calculated on the cost price.

question: The age of a mother is three times the age of her daughter. After 12 years, the mother's age will be twice the daughter's age. Find the present age of the mother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 36 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Mother's present age = 3 × daughter's present age. After 12 years, mother's age = 2 × daughter's age.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let daughter's present age = x, so mother's present age = 3x.

 

• After 12 years: 3x + 12 = 2(x + 12).

 

• 3x + 12 = 2x + 24 ⇒ x = 12.

 

• Mother's present age = 3 × 12 = 36 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up two simple linear equations in one variable (daughter's age) using the given ratios/conditions at two different points in time, then solve directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always add the same number of years to both people's ages when moving forward in time — a very common source of error is adding it to only one person.

question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 3, 6 and 4 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• A does the work in 3 days, B in 6 days, C in 4 days. Find time to complete 3 times the work together.

 

SOLUTION

 

• A's 1-day work = 1/3, B's 1-day work = 1/6, C's 1-day work = 1/4.

 

• Combined 1-day work = 1/3 + 1/6 + 1/4 = (4 + 2 + 3)/12 = 9/12 = 3/4 of the work per day.

 

• Time to complete 1 work = 1 ÷ (3/4) = 4/3 days.

 

• Time to complete 3 times the work = 3 × 4/3 = 4 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Total time for n times the work = n × (time for 1 unit of work together); no need to separately recompute combined rate for larger quantities of the same type of work.

 

NOTE

 

• Always add individual work rates (fractions of work per day), never the number of days directly, when combining workers.

question: ₹567 is divided among Arjun, Nisha and Gaurav in such a way that if ₹10, ₹45 and ₹39 are deducted from their respective shares, they have money in the ratio 3:6:2. Find the actual share of Nisha.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹303.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total = ₹567. After deducting ₹10 (Arjun), ₹45 (Nisha), ₹39 (Gaurav), remaining amounts are in ratio 3:6:2.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let remaining shares be 3x, 6x, 2x. Their sum = 11x.

 

• Total amount deducted = 10 + 45 + 39 = ₹94.

 

• Sum of original shares = sum of remaining shares + total deducted: 11x + 94 = 567 ⇒ 11x = 473 ⇒ x = 43.

 

• Nisha's remaining share = 6x = 6 × 43 = 258.

 

• Nisha's actual (original) share = 258 + 45 = ₹303.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• (Sum of ratio parts × x) + (sum of amounts deducted) = total sum; solve for x first, then add back only the specific person's deduction to their ratio share.

 

NOTE

 

• Add back the deducted amount to the correct person's ratio share only — a common mistake is adding it to the wrong person's amount.

question: Two trains, 295 m and 215 m in length are running in opposite directions. The first runs at the rate of 61 km/hr and the second at the rate of 47 km/hr. How long will they take to cross each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 17 seconds.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train lengths = 295 m and 215 m; speeds = 61 km/hr and 47 km/hr, in opposite directions.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since the trains move in opposite directions, relative speed = 61 + 47 = 108 km/hr.

 

• Convert to m/s: 108 × (5/18) = 30 m/s.

 

• Total distance to be covered while crossing = sum of lengths = 295 + 215 = 510 m.

 

• Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 510 ÷ 30 = 17 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For crossing between two trains: Time = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ (relative speed in m/s); opposite direction ⇒ add speeds, same direction ⇒ subtract speeds.

 

NOTE

 

• Never forget to convert km/hr to m/s (multiply by 5/18) before dividing distance (in metres) by speed.

question: 1/20 is what percentage of 2/40?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 100%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find what percentage 1/20 is of 2/40.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Simplify 2/40 = 1/20.

 

• So the question becomes: 1/20 is what % of 1/20?

 

• Percentage = (1/20 ÷ 1/20) × 100 = 1 × 100 = 100%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always simplify fractions to their lowest form first — many such questions disguise equal fractions in different forms to test careful reading.

 

NOTE

 

• A quantity is always 100% of itself; recognising 2/40 = 1/20 instantly solves this without any lengthy calculation.

question: The sides of a triangle are 77 cm, 36 cm and 85 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with the length of 36 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 77 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle sides: 77 cm, 36 cm, 85 cm; find the altitude to the side of length 36 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check if it's a right triangle: 36² + 77² = 1296 + 5929 = 7225 = 85². So this is a right-angled triangle, with legs 36 cm and 77 cm, and hypotenuse 85 cm.

 

• Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 36 × 77 = 1,386 cm² (using the two legs as base and height).

 

• Now, taking 36 cm as the base, the corresponding altitude (h) satisfies: Area = ½ × 36 × h ⇒ 1,386 = 18h ⇒ h = 77 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In a right triangle, the two legs are always the altitudes corresponding to each other, since the angle between them is 90° — so the altitude to one leg is simply the other leg's length.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check for a Pythagorean triplet relation among the given sides first (here 36-77-85 is a multiple of 12-25 combinations) — it hugely simplifies area and altitude calculations.

question: If 20% of 90% of 5/9 of a number is 345, find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 3450.

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of 90% of (5/9) of a number N = 345.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 20% of 90% = 0.20 × 0.90 = 0.18.

 

• 0.18 × (5/9) = (0.18 × 5)/9 = 0.9/9 = 0.1.

 

• So 0.1 × N = 345 ⇒ N = 345 ÷ 0.1 = 3450.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine all the percentage/fraction multipliers into a single decimal factor first (here 0.1), then simply divide the given value by that factor to get the number.

 

NOTE

 

• Converting fractions to decimals (5/9 stays as is until multiplied) and simplifying step-by-step avoids errors from handling three operations at once.

question: The wages of 5 carpenters for a 2-day week are ₹1,220. What are the 1-day wages (in ₹) of one carpenter?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 122.

 

GIVEN

 

• Wages of 5 carpenters for 2 days = ₹1,220.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Wages of 5 carpenters for 1 day = 1,220 ÷ 2 = ₹610.

 

• Wages of 1 carpenter for 1 day = 610 ÷ 5 = ₹122.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Total wages ÷ (number of workers × number of days) directly gives the wage of one worker for one day: 1,220 ÷ (5×2) = 1,220 ÷ 10 = 122.

 

NOTE

 

• Always divide out both the number of people and the number of days to reach a 'per person per day' rate.

question:
Simplify the following.

(√6 × √15 − 5√10) + 3√10
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. √10.

 

GIVEN

 

• (√6 × √15 − 5√10) + 3√10.

 

SOLUTION

 

• √6 × √15 = √(6 × 15) = √90 = √(9 × 10) = 3√10.

 

• Expression becomes: (3√10 − 5√10) + 3√10.

 

• = −2√10 + 3√10 = √10.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Multiply surds under a common root first (√a × √b = √(ab)), then factor out perfect squares to simplify before combining like surd terms.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 'like surds' (same number under the root) can be directly added or subtracted — always simplify each surd to its simplest form first.

question: If x² + 1/x² = 123, then a possible value of (x − 1/x) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 11.

 

GIVEN

 

• x² + 1/x² = 123.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the identity: (x − 1/x)² = x² − 2 + 1/x² = (x² + 1/x²) − 2.

 

• (x − 1/x)² = 123 − 2 = 121.

 

• x − 1/x = √121 = 11.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise: (x − 1/x)² = (x² + 1/x²) − 2, and (x + 1/x)² = (x² + 1/x²) + 2 — these two identities solve almost all such algebra questions instantly.

 

NOTE

 

• Since (x − 1/x)² = 121, the value could technically be +11 or −11; among the options, 11 is the possible value listed.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. AE-HD.

 

GIVEN

 

• Letter-cluster pairs: JN-QL, AE-HD, DH-KF, GK-NI.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Assign positions (A=1...Z=26) and check the shift from the first cluster to the second, letter by letter.

 

• JN-QL: J(10)→Q(17) = +7; N(14)→L(12) = −2.

 

• DH-KF: D(4)→K(11) = +7; H(8)→F(6) = −2.

 

• GK-NI: G(7)→N(14) = +7; K(11)→I(9) = −2.

 

• AE-HD: A(1)→H(8) = +7; E(5)→D(4) = −1 (breaks the pattern; should be −2).

 

• Three pairs follow the (+7, −2) rule; AE-HD follows (+7, −1), so it does not belong.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert letters to numbers and check the numeric shift for both positions in each pair — the odd one will break the consistent shift pattern seen in the other three.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify both letters of a two-letter cluster separately; an odd pair often matches the pattern in one letter but not the other.

question: Seven boxes B, C, D, I, J, K and L are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept between J and B. Only K is kept above I. Only two boxes are kept between K and J. C is kept at some place below L but at some place above D. How many boxes are kept between C and L?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Seven boxes B, C, D, I, J, K, L stacked; number positions 1 (top) to 7 (bottom).

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only K is kept above I' ⇒ exactly one box (K) is above I ⇒ K = 1, I = 2.

 

• 'Only two boxes are kept between K and J' ⇒ J's position − K's position − 1 = 2 ⇒ J = 1 + 3 = 4.

 

• 'Only two boxes are kept between J and B' ⇒ testing B below J: B's position − J's position − 1 = 2 ⇒ B = 4 + 3 = 7.

 

• Remaining positions 3, 5, 6 are for C, D, L. Given 'C is below L but above D' ⇒ order (top to bottom): L, then C, then D ⇒ L = 3, C = 5, D = 6.

 

• Final stack (top to bottom): K(1), I(2), L(3), J(4), C(5), D(6), B(7).

 

• Boxes between C(5) and L(3): only position 4, i.e., J — that is one box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In stacking puzzles, fix the box with the most restrictive clue first ('only X above Y' fixes exact positions), then work outward using the 'boxes between' clues.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only two boxes between P and Q' always means exactly two boxes lie strictly between their positions — don't confuse this with a difference of exactly two positions.

question:
Raman starts from Point A and drives 44 km towards east. He then takes a right turn, drives 20 km, turns right and drives 52 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 30 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 8 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again?

(Note: All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 10 km to the south.

 

GIVEN

 

• Starting at A(0,0): East 44 km, then four consecutive right turns with distances 20 km, 52 km, 30 km, 8 km.

 

SOLUTION

 

• East 44 km: (0,0) → (44, 0).

 

• Right turn from East = South; South 20 km: (44, 0) → (44, −20).

 

• Right turn from South = West; West 52 km: (44, −20) → (−8, −20).

 

• Right turn from West = North; North 30 km: (−8, −20) → (−8, 10).

 

• Right turn from North = East; East 8 km: (−8, 10) → (0, 10). This is point P.

 

• P = (0, 10), A = (0, 0). Distance = |10 − 0| = 10 km. Since P is north of A, Raman must travel south to reach A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track net displacement using coordinates (East/West as x-axis, North/South as y-axis); the final answer is simply the straight-line distance and direction back to the origin.

 

NOTE

 

• Each successive 'right turn' rotates the direction of travel by 90° clockwise: East→South→West→North→East, and so on.

question:
Refer to the given number series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

(Left) 8 4 1 9 2 5 8 1 4 6 8 7 2 4 1 6 8 7 2 6 4 9 3 5 1 7 1 (Right)

How many such even numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 8 4 1 9 2 5 8 1 4 6 8 7 2 4 1 6 8 7 2 6 4 9 3 5 1 7 1.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for an even number with an odd number immediately before AND an odd number immediately after it.

 

• Position 5: '...9, 2, 5...' → 2 is even, preceded by 9 (odd), followed by 5 (odd). Match 1.

 

• Position 7: '...5, 8, 1...' → 8 is even, preceded by 5 (odd), followed by 1 (odd). Match 2.

 

• Checking the rest of the series (positions 2, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21), no other even number has odd numbers on both sides.

 

• Total matches = Two.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write the series in a row and just underline every 'odd-even-odd' triplet as you scan left to right once — this avoids missing or double-counting any number.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check both neighbours (left AND right) before counting a match — checking only one side is the most common mistake in these series questions.

question:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

81 × 9 − 11 ÷ 2 + 6 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 25.

 

GIVEN

 

• Original equation: 81 × 9 − 11 ÷ 2 + 6 = ?; swap + ↔ − and × ↔ ÷.

 

SOLUTION

 

• After interchanging symbols: × becomes ÷, ÷ becomes ×, − becomes +, + becomes −.

 

• New expression: 81 ÷ 9 + 11 × 2 − 6.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 81 ÷ 9 = 9; 11 × 2 = 22.

 

• 9 + 22 − 6 = 31 − 6 = 25.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First rewrite the entire equation with the new (swapped) symbols on paper before calculating — solving directly in your head risks reverting to the original operators by habit.

 

NOTE

 

• After substitution, BODMAS still applies normally to the new expression — solve × /÷ before +/−.

question: HM 16 is related to JQ 19 in a certain way. In the same way, CH 22 is related to EL 25. To which of the given options is MR 27 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. OV 30.

 

GIVEN

 

• HM 16 → JQ 19; CH 22 → EL 25; find the pattern and apply it to MR 27.

 

SOLUTION

 

• HM→JQ: H(8)→J(10) = +2; M(13)→Q(17) = +4; number 16→19 = +3.

 

• CH→EL: C(3)→E(5) = +2; H(8)→L(12) = +4; number 22→25 = +3.

 

• Consistent rule: first letter +2, second letter +4, number +3.

 

• Apply to MR 27: M(13)+2 = 15 = O; R(18)+4 = 22 = V; 27+3 = 30.

 

• Result: OV 30.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Break the coded pair into 'letter1, letter2, number' and find the individual shift for each component separately — most such analogies use a fixed, simple shift for each part.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the found rule against BOTH given example pairs before applying it to the answer choice — one match could be a coincidence.

question:
Aasish starts from point A and drives 62 km towards west. He then takes a right turn, drives 58 km, turns right and drives 64 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 78 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 2 km and stops at point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach point A again?

(Note: All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 20 km to the north.

 

GIVEN

 

• Starting at A(0,0): West 62 km, then four consecutive right turns with distances 58 km, 64 km, 78 km, 2 km.

 

SOLUTION

 

• West 62 km: (0,0) → (−62, 0).

 

• Right turn from West = North; North 58 km: (−62, 0) → (−62, 58).

 

• Right turn from North = East; East 64 km: (−62, 58) → (2, 58).

 

• Right turn from East = South; South 78 km: (2, 58) → (2, −20).

 

• Right turn from South = West; West 2 km: (2, −20) → (0, −20). This is point P.

 

• P = (0, −20), A = (0, 0). Distance = |−20 − 0| = 20 km. Since P is south of A, Aasish must travel north to reach A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track net displacement with coordinates just as in the earlier direction question — the sequence of turns from West is West→North→East→South→West (each right turn rotates 90° clockwise).

 

NOTE

 

• The final direction to return is always opposite to the direction from A to P — since P is south of A, one must go north to get back.

question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single digit numbers only. Counting to be done from left to right,

(Left) 9 3 2 2 4 6 1 7 7 5 8 7 6 9 5 2 4 7 8 5 3 7 8 4 2 6 7 (Right)

How many such odd numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 9 3 2 2 4 6 1 7 7 5 8 7 6 9 5 2 4 7 8 5 3 7 8 4 2 6 7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for an odd number with odd numbers immediately before AND after it.

 

• Position 8: '...1, 7, 7...' → 7, preceded by 1 (odd), followed by 7 (odd). Match 1.

 

• Position 9: '...7, 7, 5...' → 7, preceded by 7 (odd), followed by 5 (odd). Match 2.

 

• Position 21: '...5, 3, 7...' → 3, preceded by 5 (odd), followed by 7 (odd). Match 3.

 

• No other odd number in the series has odd numbers on both sides.

 

• Total matches = 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every 'odd-odd-odd' consecutive triplet in one left-to-right scan; the middle term of each such triplet is a valid match.

 

NOTE

 

• Consecutive matches (like positions 8 and 9 sharing the number 7 at position 9) are both valid and must be counted separately, not merged.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the daughter of B',

A − B means 'A is the brother of B',

A x B means 'A is the wife of B',

A ÷ B means 'A is the father of B'.

Based on the above, how is D related to J if 'D + F − G x H ÷ J'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Mother's brother's daughter.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: '+' = daughter of; '−' = brother of; '×' = wife of; '÷' = father of. Expression: D + F − G × H ÷ J.

 

SOLUTION

 

• D + F ⇒ D is the daughter of F.

 

• F − G ⇒ F is the brother of G.

 

• G × H ⇒ G is the wife of H.

 

• H ÷ J ⇒ H is the father of J.

 

• Since H is J's father and G is H's wife, G is J's mother. Since F is G's brother, F is J's maternal uncle (mother's brother).

 

• D is F's daughter, so D is the daughter of J's maternal uncle, i.e., D is J's Mother's brother's daughter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Decode the chain one symbol at a time from left to right into plain-English relations, then build a small family tree — trying to solve it all mentally leads to errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember: a person's father's wife = mother, and a mother's brother = maternal uncle (mama) — these two deductions are key to solving this puzzle.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ORL.

 

GIVEN

 

• Letter-clusters: ORL, GJC, ILE, LOH.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the letter-to-letter shift within each cluster using positions (A=1...Z=26).

 

• GJC: G(7)→J(10) = +3; J(10)→C(3) = −7.

 

• ILE: I(9)→L(12) = +3; L(12)→E(5) = −7.

 

• LOH: L(12)→O(15) = +3; O(15)→H(8) = −7.

 

• ORL: O(15)→R(18) = +3; R(18)→L(12) = −6 (should be −7 to match the pattern).

 

• Three clusters follow the (+3, −7) rule; ORL follows (+3, −6), so it is the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert to positional numbers and check both the first-to-second and second-to-third letter shifts — the odd cluster will deviate in one of the two shifts.

 

NOTE

 

• Even a shift of just 1 unit different from the pattern (here −6 instead of −7) is enough to make a cluster the odd one out.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(24, 480, 10)

(12, 552, 23)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. (4, 80, 10).

 

GIVEN

 

• Sets: (24, 480, 10) and (12, 552, 23) share a hidden logic; find the matching option set.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test: middle number = 2 × (first number) × (third number).

 

• Check set 1: 2 × 24 × 10 = 480 ✓ (matches given middle number).

 

• Check set 2: 2 × 12 × 23 = 552 ✓ (matches given middle number).

 

• Apply the rule to each option: (13,293,11): 2×13×11 = 286 ≠ 293 ✗. (4,80,10): 2×4×10 = 80 ✓. (19,691,18): 2×19×18 = 684 ≠ 691 ✗. (11,51,2): 2×11×2 = 44 ≠ 51 ✗.

 

• Only (4, 80, 10) satisfies the rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With two given number sets, first hunt for a simple relation like sum, product, or 'middle = k × first × third' by testing small multipliers (×2, ×3...) — most such series use a single simple formula.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the discovered formula against BOTH given sets before testing the options, to avoid a rule that only coincidentally fits one set.

question: If 1 is added to each even digit and 2 is subtracted from each odd digit in the number 7894562, what will be the sum of the digits which are second from the left and second from the right in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 16.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 7894562. Rule: add 1 to each even digit, subtract 2 from each odd digit.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Digit-by-digit: 7(odd)→7−2=5; 8(even)→8+1=9; 9(odd)→9−2=7; 4(even)→4+1=5; 5(odd)→5−2=3; 6(even)→6+1=7; 2(even)→2+1=3.

 

• New number: 5 9 7 5 3 7 3.
